tldr: This is a weekend catch-up run covering Friday's full US/Asia close: the Fed's hawkish turn is now confirmed by a SECOND data point in three days -- Oct core PPI (released Fri) matched an already-hot 0.3% m/m consensus with PPI y/y hitting 6.5% (~4yr high), on top of Monday's hot core CPI, pushing a chorus of Fed speakers (Logan, Collins, Daly, Bowman) toward a now-100%-priced December hike (~88.5% 25bp / ~11.5% 50bp).

Nvidia closed Friday below $4T market cap, its sixth straight weekly decline (-12.75%, worst run since 2012) following CEO Jensen Huang's Nov 12 resignation -- dragging Hang Seng tech (Tencent -3.1%, Xiaomi -3.7%) even as a new Senate Banking probe into Commerce Secretary Lutnick's chip-export oversight surfaced a Singapore angle (Megaspeed, a $4.8B+ Nvidia buyer with a China-tied executive under scrutiny).

Levered silver extended its slide (-2.2% Friday to ~$49 spot) even as gold stabilized (~flat, holding $3,890-3,915) -- a genuine divergence within the precious-metals complex worth watching alongside the code-owned risk calc's margin-distance tracking.

China confirmed (MOFCOM, 9 Nov) its rare-earth/export-control truce extends through 10 Jan 2027 -- the one clear structural de-escalation data point this week, cooling the near-term scarcity catalyst for MP/Lynas/USAR even as MP itself posted a standalone beat (Q3 revenue +176% y/y on GM magnet-qualification ramp, insiders buying $3.35M).

Hong Kong's Southbound mainland buying extended to a 5th straight session and Korea's foreign-institutional buying streak broke (foreigners sold -₩703.3bn Friday, ending a 3-day run) on the Nvidia-linked risk-off tape -- a reminder that Friday's selloff was broad enough to interrupt even the more persistent regional flows.

Congress trades refreshed with a much fresher set (Oct 1-Nov 5, 11 distinct members) after the prior file had gone stale to late Oct -- the biggest cluster is four members' mechanical WBD merger cash-outs, plus a genuine new SGX insider catch: MPACT's manager took part of its Q3 fee in units (13 Nov, lifting its stake 3.10%->3.17%).

regime.label: Hawkish hiking cycle confirmed by sticky core inflation; fragile but orderly risk-on
regime.oneLiner: A now fully-priced December Fed hike, confirmed by back-to-back hot CPI and PPI prints and a broad Fed hawkish chorus, is being absorbed in orderly fashion by equities (a weekly loss, not a disorderly risk-off move) while precious metals diverge and China's rare-earth truce extension offers the week's one clear de-escalation.

topNews.headline: Nvidia closes below $4T market cap, posts sixth straight weekly decline (-12.75%) -- longest losing streak since 2012
topNews.actionable: The AI-bellwether's compounding leadership-and-valuation shock is dragging HK tech (Tencent -3.1%, Xiaomi -3.7% Friday) by sentiment contagion even without direct linkage -- keep the HK tech book hedged into Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings call rather than reading the HK selloff as fundamentally China-specific.

topNews.headline: US October PPI: headline misses at +0.3% (vs +0.4% forecast), core in line at +0.3%, but y/y hits 6.5% -- highest since 2022
topNews.actionable: A second straight confirming inflation print behind Monday's hot CPI cements the December hike as data-driven, not just Fed-speak -- the 1.6x levered silver position's margin-call distance should be assumed to keep compressing until the Dec 8-9 FOMC resolves the 25bp-vs-50bp tail.

topNews.headline: Weekend crypto crash: Bitcoin breaks below $70K to ~$67.5K on $1.64B liquidation wave; Ethereum under $2,000
topNews.actionable: Crypto is trading as the highest-beta expression of the hawkish-Fed repricing with no idiosyncratic offset this weekend -- a level, not a settled close (markets trade 24/7), worth rechecking at the Monday Asia open before drawing conclusions.

topNews.headline: China extends rare-earth export-control suspension to January 10, 2027; dysprosium/terbium/yttrium curbs stay in force
topNews.actionable: Confirms the Nov 9 truce read -- cools the near-term scarcity catalyst for the ex-China rare-earth basket (MP, Lynas, USAR) even as MP's own Q3 beat (+176% revenue, insider buying) argues the re-shoring thesis doesn't need a crisis to work; Jan 10, 2027 is the next hard deadline.

topNews.headline: Commerce Secretary Lutnick agrees to testify over Nvidia chip-export oversight tied to Singapore-based Megaspeed
topNews.actionable: A Singapore-domiciled buyer is now at the center of a US chip-export enforcement probe -- a jurisdiction-specific headline risk worth tracking given the book's SGX concentration, even though none of the held SGX names are directly implicated.

signals: No model call currently clears the pUp3m >=0.6/<=0.4 with confidence >=0.55 bar this run -- the closest directional read is TLT (pUp3m 0.39, ev3m -0.035) at only moderate confidence (0.45), consistent with a regime that's directionally hawkish on duration but not high-conviction on any single asset.

The WBD merger cash-out cluster (Pelosi, Kustoff, Johnson, Cisneros, all dated Oct 7) is this run's cleanest multi-member convergence -- mechanical, not a trading signal, but a useful reminder of how often a single corporate event shows up simultaneously across unrelated members' disclosures.

NVDA: congressional buying (Salazar, Oct 23) predates the Huang resignation by three weeks -- a timing coincidence -- while retail is the more active current counterparty, having bought a reported $1.6B of NVDA over three sessions through Nov 12; consider watching the Nov 17 earnings call under interim CEO Colette Kress as the next hard catalyst.

A chip-equipment congressional convergence (Gottheimer rebuying AMAT Oct 26, Taylor buying AVGO/LRCX in early Nov) lines up with a sector that fell 20-26% over the trailing month before a sharp one-session rebound on Nov 11 -- worth watching whether the rebound holds into AMAT's reported earnings.

Rare-earth basket: confirmed truce extension keeps pUp3m clustered 0.51-0.56 at low-to-moderate confidence (0.24-0.38) across the 9-ticker basket -- no single name clears a high-conviction bar, consistent with a cooled rather than resolved catalyst.
